messages.subject: [rkward-users] [Help] RE: workspace doesn't save layout (scripts)
messages.body_plain:
The following forum message was posted by tfry at http://sourceforge.net/projects/rkward/forums/forum/165574/topic/4857688:

Hi!

First, please check Settings->Configure RKWard->General. There are several options
on how to save the workplace layout. Make sure, this is set to "Save/restore
with R workspace, when saving/loading R workspace".

If that does not help, look out for a file in the same directory as your saved
workspace, with the same file name, but an appended ".rkworkplace". Does this
file exist (if the above option is set, it should be created when you save the
workspace)? Open it in a text editor. Does it appear to contain the relevant
script files?

Regards
Thomas

messages.body_plain:
The following forum message was posted by tfry at http://sourceforge.net/projects/rkward/forums/forum/165574/topic/4857688:

Several workspaces in the same directory should not be a problem. But please
test, whether it works, when saving to a different directory. Perhaps there
is a problem with the permissions to create files in that dir?

Please take a look at the "Command log" window. When saving, you should see
a call to rk.save.workplace() before the call to save(). Is that present? Are
there any errors attached to that? What if you copy and paste the call
to rk.save.workplace() to the R Console window?

Does rk.get.workspace.url() yield the correct result?

Regards
Thomas

strange.

thanks !

messages.subject: [rkward-users] new external plugin: cluster analysis
messages.body_plain:
hi,

i've been on some trains again... as suggested by burfee earlier, i tried to 
write GUI dialogs for most of
 o http://statmethods.net/advstats/cluster.html
it's not complete (only used base and mclust functions), but still the most 
important features should be available now:
 o http://rkward.sourceforge.net/R/pckg/rk.ClusterAnalysis/index.html

you need RKWard 0.5.7, where you can easily install the plugin via the R 
package management dialog ("rk.ClusterAnalysis"). after installation, you 
should find "Cluster analysis" sub menus in "Analysis" and "Plots". note that 
i put the usual plot functions in the "Analysis" dialogs at the moment, as 
this seemed to me to be the most comfortable workflow (especially using the 
preview feature). in the "Plots" menu is a graphical tool to determine the 
number of clusters to extract. adding to the k-means WSS method described on 
the Quick-R page, i also tried to implement a quite configurable inverse Scree 
plot -- i hope i got that one right!

so, please check it out! (see e.g. ?kmeans for sample data in the examples)

being that this is the result of two train rides, there's surely need for 
improvements and bug-fixing. btw., the plugin was (of course ;-)) developed 
with the rkwarddev package, and as usual you can find the very build script in 
the installed plugin location, if you want to change things:
 $YOUR_R_PACKAGES/rk.ClusterAnalysis/rkward/rkwarddev_CA_plugin_script.R

messages.subject: [rkward-users] Intalling multiple versions of Rkward and KDEwin
messages.subject_clean: [rkward-users] Intalling multiple versions of Rkward and KDEwin
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

On Tuesday 13 December 2011, Francois Maurice wrote:
> Is it possible to install multiple vsersions of Rkward and KDE for Windows?

yes. However, if different versions of KDE are involved, after running one 
installation, and before starting a different one, you will have to kill all 
KDE-processes, or reboot the system. If you see the message "Could not start 
process Cannot talk to klauncher: The name org.kde.klauncher was not provided 
by any .service files.", you know you have run into the problem.

This should not be a problem, if all installations use the same version of 
KDE.

Regards
Thomas
